institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The arctic context and the focus on inclusion of indigenous knowledge in landscape architecture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The whole process upon confirmation of exchange was one long rollercoaster, with confusion and contradicting messages from different institutions. This affected my whole autumn semester, which was filled with stress and insecurity. The problems were caused due to miscommunication between the mobility teams from Copenhagen University and UIT. I was several times told that the exchange was invalid from UIT, where CU refused to listen to my concerns. In the future, I hope that both mobility teams will improve their intern communication, so it is not the students responsibility to connect the dots and find the right people to ask. My final spot at UIT was only approved because I knew someone studying there, who could give me the right contact person. This is not fair for my classmates who did not get the same opportunity.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
There was an intro-week at campus, which unluckily was colliding with my first days of school. The one day I managed to join was fine, although a lot of informations were overlapping. 
The landscape architecture department was welcoming and showed me around the first day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
The orientation of UIT campus was great, but my education was located at the art academy, which was isolated from the rest of the university. 
I experienced a lack of communication between UIT and the Art Academy.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Samskipnaden has several housing opportunities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The housing is located 10 m walk from campus, with a great view of the city. The social life was minimal. My social arena was at school (The Art Academy).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great housing, but for an exchange student its very unlucky that the apartments lack appliances. I had to spend the first week looking for a bed, a fridge, a stove etc.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Just follow the link given to you by e-mail.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mail to mobility team.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Success.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contact the head of the department directly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Master level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching had less lectures, more assignments and supervisions. One large project to solve individually the whole semester. Less group work than UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Studio 2: Landscape practices
Nature perspectives

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Nature perspectives with Eimear was amazing. Great literature.

questions.answer: Engage yourself in a solidarity community like pro-palestina group. Knitting group.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
The magical landscape all around Tromsø. Take the ferry from Sommarøya for to Senja for free. Kvaløya, Ersfjordbotn. 
Tromsø Kunstforening.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: yes

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: be open.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: nothing for me personally.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: learning about the saami culture and their struggles.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be aware of your presence on colonized land. Read up on the Saami history and the Norwegianisation processes, and the ongoing struggles for the saami people of Tromsø.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the UIT Campus is very separated from the Art Academy and the city.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning about the Saami traditional knowledge and their ongoing struggles. Meeting new people. Experiencing the extreme landscapes in different seasons.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Tromsø city lack public spaces, parks and places for spontanity to occour. Loneliness could be an issue. And miss buying all sorts of vegetables and vegetarian products as a student with low cash flow.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
